answer: A staking bond with a long horizon makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after sustained honest work, so a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of bonds at once. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict and public, every attestation signed and timestamped, so sockpuppets cannot hide in noise. When the tide of cheap identities rises, the bond price rises with it, and attackers pay more to create each fake than the fake can ever earn back.
